title: Brother torn over coroner's inquest
article: The grieving brother of a man who died in police custody says he has mixed emotions about an upcoming coroner's inquest into his brother's death.

A jury will examine the death of Paul Horan, 43, during a mandatory inquest, the Ontario West Region Coroner's Office announced Tuesday. A date, location and presiding coroner have yet to be revealed.
Horan died in Lambton OPP custody after being pulled over on Highway 402, near Forest Road, on Sept. 23, 2010.
He was taken into custody around 11:30 p.m. and was pronounced dead around 2:20 a.m. after going into convulsions in the back of an officer's cruiser.

The Special Investigations Unit (SIU) didn't find the officer guilty of any criminal liability in a report released last March. Instead the report stated Horan had ingested pills and refused to pull over in a vehicle with expired plates.
Horan's brother, Dave Horan, said he doesn't agree with the SIU's findings and worries the coroner's inquest will be more of the same.
"I've heard their lies and so it's going to be no different than that," he said Tuesday.
The officer, who has never been named, declined to co-operate with the SIU investigation -- nor was he required to -- the provincial agency told Dave Horan last March.
The police account ignored physical trauma the family saw on the body, Horan said, noting his younger brother's death has been hard on the family.
"That's all my mom goes on about any more," he said. "She questions everything."
The inquest will examine all the events surrounding Paul Horan's death, said Dr. Rick Mann, regional supervising coroner for West Region.
"The purpose of the inquest is to answer five questions of who, when, where, by what means and manner, and the why of death," he said.
A jury will then be allowed to make recommendations to prevent similar deaths, Mann said.
Organizations, like the OPP, have a year to report whether or not the recommendations have been implemented. Implementation isn't required, Mann said, but a status report must still be made.
Mann said an inquest into Horan's death is mandatory, in accordance with the Coroner's Act, because he died in police custody.
Dave Horan isn't sure his family will ever have closure.
"If the truth comes out, we will get closure," he said. "But if they continue the way they are, there won't be any closure."
